origin: Introduced in the 1970s by the statistician John Tukey for exploratory data analysis. Its box and whiskers give it the name box-and-whisker plot.
whenToUse: You compare the spread of groups such as regions or weekdays.
You check for values far from the rest.
Data an average alone could misrepresent.
whenNotToUse: Showing it to people unfamiliar with box plots (use a histogram).
There are only a few values (show them all as dots).
The distribution has two or more peaks (use a histogram).

alternatives.name: Histogram
alternatives.reason: Looking closely at the shape of one group's distribution.

accessibility: Pointing at it shows the median and the middle 50% range in text.
The table view lists each group's five numbers and its outliers.
Boxes and outliers are drawn with different shapes and colors.
